title: Staggered acceptance windows and decision-escrow for cross-team PRD reviews
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Problem: PRD acceptance frequently stalls because signoff requires synchronous availability from engineering, design, and legal reviewers. This causes multi-week waits or scope creep as PMs wait for a single meeting.

Proposal: Implement a documented, enforceable 'staggered acceptance window' model and a lightweight 'decision escrow' mechanism. Key components:
- Define ordered review lanes (Design -> Eng -> Legal) with explicit timeboxes per lane (e.g., 5 business days design, 7 business days eng, 5 business days legal).
- Provide an 'Accepted with Conditions (Escrow)' state where a reviewer can record conditional approval plus required follow-ups; the escrow entry includes owner, deadline, and acceptance-impact rating.
- Create PRD template sections and Confluence forms to capture escrow entries and automated reminders.
- Async-first reviews: encourage inline comments, triage threads, and targeted meeting only when blockers remain after the window.

Trade-offs and rationale:
- Risk: Potential for rubber-stamp approvals. Mitigation: mandatory escrow fields, explicit severity levels, and spot checks by the PM review coordinator.
- Benefit: Reduced time-to-decision and clearer ownership for follow-ups; smoother rollouts and fewer last-minute scope changes.

Scope: Pilot with three product squads for 6 weeks, iterate on templates and automation, then expand org-wide.
acceptance_criteria: Pilot with at least 3 squads completes PRD signoff using the staggered model and decision escrow
Average PRD review cycle time reduced by >= 30% for pilot squads compared to previous quarter
All escrow entries include owner, deadline, mitigation plan, and severity level
PRD template and Confluence escrow form published and linked from PRD checklist
Automated reminder emails created and validated (day +3 and day -1 before lane deadline)
At least one post-pilot retro captured and updated playbook based on feedback
